title: Great Mosque of al-Nuri
visualBrief: Individual rebuilt al-Nuri mosque visualization: retained hall plan, a green central dome, four short corner turrets, pointed hall gallery, side courtyard arcades, small octagonal fountain pavilion and the separate tall northwestern brick Al-Hadba minaret. Shared low-contrast textures, original geometry, no copied photographs, inscriptions, furnished interiors or museum/visitor-center additions. The site extension and vertical proportions remain explicitly approximate.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained Q5599605 / way468118902 anchor [43.126768234,36.342740215] and heading -0.096841454998 rad remain unchanged. The six-vertex hall plan is the retained map-axis outline, not a newly extracted current building polygon. Current named mosque POI35184840207734 still says ruins; the inspected2025 pictures show rebuilt architecture. Current named Al-Hadba POI17596477684205 supplies the northwest minaret point [-36.0811989170203,-71.4911008586867]. A second Arabic minaret marker17597058803445 lies near the court center; it conflicts with the northwestern tower seen beside the hall and is retained as excluded ambiguity, not a second tall minaret. Current four-vertex garden35184869293474 constrains the east garden; courtyard arcades and narrow paths are inferred around it. Positive X east-northeast along the hall; positive Z south-southeast; the court/front faces negative Z. Site extension and lean bearing are approximations.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: No retained published height/width/length facts and no current PMTiles part heights are available. All vertical values are explicit picture/footprint-scale estimates: hall roof8.5 m, main drum10.8 m, green dome19 m/finial20.5 m, four short turret finials16.8 m, Al-Hadba finial45 m with an estimated1.6 m eastward offset, courtyard arcade eaves7 m and fountain pavilion roof6.8 m. The lean direction/magnitude are not surveyed. Gallery bay count, dome profiles, minaret bands, fountain, paving and site extension are visualization reconstruction. Retained historic=ruins is preserved verbatim rather than presented as current appearance.
